title: Implement session ID capture and resume
description:
Update the entrypoint to capture Claude's session ID from stream-json output and use it when resuming after a rate limit hit.

Capture: pipe Claude's output through a filter that reads the `init` event and saves `session_id` to `/tmp/claude-session-id`.

Resume: at the start of each Claude launch, check if `/tmp/claude-session-id` exists. If it does, add `--resume <id>` to the claude invocation and use the prompt "Continue where you left off." instead of the original prompt.

This integrates with the rate limit recovery in Phase 3 — when the scheduler re-queues a rate-limited pod and the entrypoint loop restarts Claude, it will automatically use the session resume.
acceptance_criteria: `/tmp/claude-session-id` is written within seconds of Claude starting
If the file exists when entrypoint restarts Claude, `--resume <id>` is used
Session resume is logged as a RESUMED event (once event logging is implemented in 4.3)
If session resume fails (invalid/expired session), entrypoint falls back to fresh start with original prompt
The original prompt is preserved in `/tmp/claude-initial-prompt` so fallback is possible

title: Build pod status monitor
description:
Create `agents/base-image/status-monitor.sh`, a background script that accurately tracks Claude's state and updates the pod label.

The monitor runs as a background process launched from the entrypoint. Every 10 seconds it checks:
1. Is the tmux session `claude` alive? (`tmux has-session -t claude`)
2. Is a `claude` process running? (`pgrep -f 'claude '`)
3. Does `/tmp/claude-done` exist? (set by entrypoint on exit)

State transitions:
- tmux alive + claude process running → no change (still `running`)
- tmux alive + no claude process → `waiting-input` (Claude finished, session waiting)
- tmux gone + `/tmp/claude-done` → `done` or `error` (based on exit code file)
- tmux gone + no done file → `error` (unexpected exit)

The script uses `kubectl label pod $HOSTNAME -n claude-workers <label>=<value> --overwrite` and only patches when the value changes (read current label first).
acceptance_criteria: Status monitor runs as a background process in each pod
Pod label changes to `waiting-input` when Claude finishes a response in tmux
Pod label changes to `done` when entrypoint writes /tmp/claude-done with exit code 0
Pod label changes to `error` when Claude exits unexpectedly
Monitor does not thrash labels (only patches on actual state changes)
Monitor exits cleanly when the pod is being terminated

title: Implement pod event logging
description:
Add structured event logging to the entrypoint script. Each significant lifecycle event is appended to `/workspace/.claude-events.log` in a machine-readable format.

Format: `<ISO8601 timestamp> <EVENT> [key=value ...]`

Events to log:
- `STARTED` — pod began initialization (task, repo, branch, ticket)
- `CLONED` — git clone completed (elapsed time)
- `BRANCH_CHECKED_OUT` — branch ready (branch name, created=true/false)
- `CLAUDE_STARTED` — Claude launched (session_id)
- `RATE_LIMITED` — rate limit detected (retry_after ISO8601)
- `RESUMED` — Claude resumed after rate limit (session_id)
- `CLAUDE_DONE` — Claude exited (exit_code, elapsed)
- `FOLLOW_UP` — follow-up prompt received (prompt preview, first 80 chars)
- `ERROR` — unexpected error (message)

Helper function in entrypoint:
```bash
log_event() {
  echo "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) $@" >> /workspace/.claude-events.log
}
```
acceptance_criteria: `/workspace/.claude-events.log` is created when pod starts
All listed events are written with correct format
Event log is readable via `kubectl exec -- cat /workspace/.claude-events.log`
Events include relevant key=value metadata for each event type
Log file survives across multiple Claude sessions in the same pod

title: Implement `ccw follow-up <task>`
description:
Add `ccw follow-up <task> [--prompt] <text>` subcommand to send additional instructions to Claude.

Behavior based on pod status:
- `waiting-input` (Claude at interactive prompt): send text directly to tmux:
  ```bash
  kubectl exec -n claude-workers <pod> -- \
    tmux send-keys -t claude "<escaped-prompt>" Enter
  ```
- `running` (Claude actively working): write to follow-up queue file in pod:
  ```bash
  kubectl exec -n claude-workers <pod> -- \
    bash -c "echo '<prompt>' >> /tmp/follow-up-queue"
  ```
  The entrypoint picks up queued follow-ups after Claude finishes.
- `done` or `stopped`: resume Claude with the follow-up as a new session start:
  ```bash
  # Send to tmux which will start a new claude run
  kubectl exec -n claude-workers <pod> -- \
    tmux send-keys -t claude "claude --resume $(cat /tmp/claude-session-id) '<prompt>'" Enter
  ```
- `error` / `rate-limited` / `queued`: print error with explanation

Also append a FOLLOW_UP event to the event log.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw follow-up <task> "add unit tests"` sends prompt to waiting-input Claude
Follow-up while running queues the message for after current response
Follow-up on a done pod resumes Claude with session ID
Error message explains why follow-up isn't possible for rate-limited/queued pods
FOLLOW_UP event is written to the event log

title: Implement `ccw history`
description:
Add two variants of event history:

`ccw history <task>` — show all events for a specific task:
```
2024-03-15 10:00:00  STARTED        task=my-app-20240315-a3f9
2024-03-15 10:00:05  CLONED         elapsed=5s
2024-03-15 10:00:06  BRANCH_READY   branch=feat/login created=false
2024-03-15 10:00:07  CLAUDE_STARTED session=abc123
2024-03-15 14:32:10  RATE_LIMITED   retry=2024-03-15T19:32:10Z
2024-03-15 19:32:15  RESUMED        session=abc123
2024-03-15 20:45:00  CLAUDE_DONE    exit=0 elapsed=1h12m
```

Fetch via `kubectl exec -n claude-workers <pod> -- cat /workspace/.claude-events.log`.

`ccw history` (no args) — aggregate recent events across all pods, last 50 events sorted by time:
```
[my-app-20240315-a3f9]  10:00:00  STARTED
[other-20240314-b8c2]   10:02:00  CLAUDE_DONE exit=0
...
```
acceptance_criteria: `ccw history <task>` prints all events from that pod's event log
`ccw history` aggregates recent events across all running/recent pods
Timestamps are formatted readably (not raw Unix timestamps)
Error if task doesn't exist or event log is not found (pod too new)
Events are color-coded by type (STARTED=blue, DONE=green, ERROR=red, RATE_LIMITED=yellow)

title: Implement `ccw feedback <task>`
description:
Add `ccw feedback <task> <message>` as a high-level workflow command for the human review loop.

This command is designed for the flow where:
1. Claude pushed some commits
2. Human pulled the branch and tested it locally
3. Human has specific feedback to send back

The command:
1. Fetches and displays task metadata:
   ```
   Task:     my-app-20240315-a3f9
   Branch:   feat/login
   Latest:   abc1234 - "Add login form validation" (2 commits pushed)
   Status:   done
   ```
   (Branch/commit info from `kubectl exec -- git -C /workspace/<repo> log --oneline -3`)
2. Sends the message as a follow-up (delegates to `ccw follow-up` internally)
3. Prints connection instructions: "Claude is working on your feedback. Connect with: ccw ssh <task>"

Also support `ccw feedback <task>` (no message) to open an editor for longer feedback.
acceptance_criteria: `ccw feedback <task> "fix the tests"` shows branch info then sends feedback
Latest commit info is shown (fetched from git inside the pod)
Feedback is sent as a follow-up prompt to Claude
`ccw feedback <task>` (no message) opens $EDITOR for multi-line feedback
Output confirms that Claude is working and how to connect
